summary:
Minas Gerais ranked 2nd nationally in 2024 with 12 killings and tied for the top in 2025 with 8 (matching Ceará). Against a population of ~21 million, the 2025 rate of ~0.38/million sits at the national average, but the consistency of appearing in the top two every year signals a structurally elevated environment compared with states that fluctuate. The 2024 total of 12 placed it behind only São Paulo.

These factors put Minas Gerais about 0.07 below the national 0.71. Compared with Ceará (0.61), which matched the same 2025 absolute count on a much smaller population, Minas Gerais' per-capita exposure is roughly half—so the deviation is more moderate. Compared with São Paulo (no deviation recorded), which led the 2024 count at 16 but fell sharply in 2025, Minas Gerais' consistency across both years is the distinguishing risk factor.

No state-specific legal restriction or unique ordinance was identified. The risk for a visitor is violence-exposure, patterned over two years, in a large interior state where the 68%-outside-capitals finding of the 2024 dossier implies added danger away from Belo Horizonte.

sources.summary: Sergipe em Debate write-up (updated 27 Jan 2025) of the Antra dossier for 2024: 122 trans and travesti killings, 16% below 2023's 145 and under the 2008-2024 average of 125/yr; worst states São Paulo 16, Minas Gerais 12, Ceará 11; no records found in Acre, Rio Grande do Norte or Roraima in 2024; at least 68% (83 cases) occurred in interior cities outside state capitals; 95.9% of victims travestis/trans women; chronic official under-notification criticised by Antra.

SBT News report (26 Jan 2026) on the 9th edition of the ANTRA dossier: Brazil recorded 80 killings of trans and travesti people in 2025, down 34% on 2024, still the world's highest; state counts for 2025 - Ceará and Minas Gerais 8 each, Bahia and Pernambuco 7, Goiás/Maranhão/Pará 5, Paraíba, Paraná, Rio Grande do Norte and São Paulo 4 each, Mato Grosso and Rio de Janeiro 3, Alagoas, Distrito Federal, Espírito Santo and Mato Grosso do Sul 2; 1,261 killings 2017-2025 (~140/yr); 97% of victims travestis/trans women, 70% Black, 67.5% committed outside state capitals.
